title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 131-132). Grothendieck is in the part of the 1965 'Galois theory of motives' notes that classifies Weil numbers, presumably to describe the motivic Galois group over a finite field F_Q through its Frobenius elements. The ambient objects are a totally real number field K, a CM field L (a totally imaginary quadratic extension of K), and a rational Q > 1.

What the previous page establishes:
- An element λ with λλ̄ = Q (equivalently, all |σ(λ)|² = Q) is determined by a = λ + λ̄ ∈ K together with the condition 4Q − a² ≫ 0 (totally positive).
- The 'Remarque' starts from any a ∈ K with K = Q(a). It chooses i large enough that 4Q^i − a² is totally positive and lets λ be a root of T² − aT + Q^i.
- Then L = K(λ) is a totally imaginary quadratic extension of K, generated by λ, with |λ|² = Q^i. If Q and a are integral, λ is an algebraic integer.

This page tries to remove the exponent i. It asserts that λ' = λ^{1/i} 'will also be in L', with a garbled justification ('car λλ̄ = Q..., et on a pris ses conjugués...'). It concludes that there is λ' ∈ L with λ'λ̄' = |λ'|² = Q such that Q(λ') is (totally) imaginary and contains K. If Q is an integer, λ' can be taken integral.

In modern terms, the intended statement is: for every totally real K and every Q > 1 there is a Weil Q-number (of weight 1) λ' whose field Q(λ') is a CM field containing K, with λ' integral when Q ∈ Z. This is the kind of existence statement needed to show that every totally real field, and many CM fields, occur as centres or Frobenius fields of motives over F_Q. Compare Honda–Tate theory, and the description of the motivic Galois group over F_q via the group of Weil numbers (later Milne, Langlands–Rapoport).

The text breaks off here. The next page begins a different topic (groups G, G_1, objects M).
errors:
The key step 'λ^{1/i} sera aussi dans L' is false in general. Counterexample: take K = Q and Q = 2.
- An element λ' of an imaginary quadratic field with |λ'|² = 2 has trace a' ∈ Z with a'² < 8.
- So the only imaginary quadratic fields generated by such a λ' are Q(i) (a' = ±2), Q(√−2) (a' = 0) and Q(√−7) (a' = ±1).
- The construction of the previous page gives L = Q(√(a² − 4·2^i)), which for suitable a and i is any of infinitely many other fields.
- In those fields no i-th root of λ exists, and no element of absolute value √2 exists at all.
The justification given ('on a pris ses conjugués...') does not support the claim.

The final existence statement can be rescued, but not by this route. In the non-integral case: take a ∈ K with K = Q(a), scale a by a small rational so that |σ(a)| < 2√Q for all σ, and take λ' a root of T² − aT + Q. In the integral case one needs a totally real algebraic integer generating a field containing K, with all conjugates in (−2√Q, 2√Q). This requires an approximation or Fekete–Szegő/Robinson type argument (the interval has length > 4 since Q ≥ 2), not an i-th root.
With the root-extraction argument, the conclusion 'Q(λ') contains K' is unjustified. Even when λ' exists, Q(λ') could be a proper subfield of L.

ideas.what: Elements of a CM field with λλ̄ = Q (all archimedean absolute values √Q), parametrized by a = λ + λ̄ totally real with 4Q − a² ≫ 0
Existence, for any totally real K and Q > 1, of a Weil Q-number generating a CM field containing K (integral if Q ∈ Z)
ideas.modern_name: realisation of totally real/CM fields as Frobenius fields of motives over F_q (cf. Honda–Tate)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Honda–Tate theory; Milne on motives over finite fields

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine auxiliary lemma about Weil numbers in CM fields, and the extraction-of-roots step is actually wrong. It is of mild historical interest as an early (1965, pre-Honda–Tate) look at which CM fields arise as Frobenius fields in a Galois theory of motives, but there is nothing new for specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the parenthesis reads '(car λλ̄ = Q ∈ ..., et on a ... pris ses conjugués...)'. The symbol after Q looks like a struck/unfinished '∈', probably meant as 'Q ∈ Q' or 'Q^i'.
Line 3: before 'λ'λ̄'' there is a struck symbol (looks like 'γ'). The formula reads 'avec λ'λ̄' = |λ'|² = Q'.
Line 4: '(totalement)' is inserted above a crossed-out 'pur'. The text reads 'Q(λ') soit (totalement) imaginaire et contienne K', with 'contienne' underlined.
